hero.title: Economic Engine of Gupta Empire
hero.description: An analysis of the agrarian, commercial, and fiscal foundations that defined the 'Golden Age' of Gupta rule.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Key shifts in the Gupta economic landscape from rise to decentralization.

cards.details: Consolidation of trade routes and stabilization of currency under Chandragupta I.
Prosperity under Chandragupta II; high volume of maritime trade and expansion of land grants.
Economic decline marked by Huna invasions and the transition to a more localized, feudal economy.

items.title: C.A.G.E
items.decryption: Use this to recall the pillars: C-Cess (Udranga/Uparikara), A-Agrarian (Land classification), G-Guilds (Sreni), E-Exports (Maritime trade).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Assumption that the 'Golden Age' meant high taxation; in reality, tax rates were relatively moderate compared to Mauryan times.
Confusing 'Agrahara' (land grants to Brahmins) with 'Devadana' (grants to temples); distinguish these clearly.
Assuming a fully money-based economy; the Gupta period saw an increase in land-based transactions and a decline in gold coin circulation in the later stages.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Gangetic Plains as the agrarian heartland.
  • Ports: Tamralipti (East) and Bharuch (West).
  • Resource zones: Chota Nagpur (iron/copper).

Key Sectors

  • Sreni (Guilds): Managed prices, wages, and banking.
  • Land Grants: Emergence of Proto-feudalism.
  • Coinage: Dinaras (Gold) and Rupaka (Silver).

Economic Structure Mindmap

  • Agrarian Base:
    • Classification: Kshetra (arable), Khila (barren), Aprahata (forest).
    • Taxation: Bhaga (share), Bhoga (periodic supplies), Udranga (fixed tax).
  • Trade & Guilds:
    • Sreni autonomy: Own seals and laws, acted as local banks.
    • Exports: Spices, ivory, silk, precious stones.
TermMeaning
AgraharaLand grant to Brahmins
VishtiForced labor (increasingly common)
DinarasStandard Gold coins
